script: The US Navy rejected Hedy Lamarr's invention because she was just an actress. In 1942, the Hollywood star co-invented a radio guidance system that hopped between frequencies so fast, enemies couldn't jam it. She patented it, handed it to the Navy for free, and expected them to use it to save lives. Officials looked at the patent, then looked at her name, and decided a movie star could not possibly understand real engineering. They told her to go sell war bonds instead, and shelved the invention completely. Decades later, the military quietly built the exact same technology and used it during the Cuban Missile Crisis, without ever crediting her. That same idea eventually became the foundation of WiFi, GPS, and Bluetooth. The Navy rejected her invention for being just an actress, and used it anyway once nobody remembered whose idea it was.
